claims.subject: hydrodeoxygenation
claims.evidence_text: The conversion of UCO increases with an increase in the acidity of the support [23,24]. NiMo/ γ-Al2O3 (CAT A) prepared using alumina as the support is less active and therefore shows less conversion of UCO. The conversion of UCO increases from 80 % on CAT A to 85 and 87 % on catalysts NiMo/Al2O3-SiO2 (90:10) (CAT B) & NiMo/Al2O3-SiO2 (70:30) (CAT C) respectively prepared with alumina-silica as the support. This is because alumina-silica supports are more acidic than pure gamma-alumina supports. The distribution of various fractions obtained from SIMDIST analysis is also shown in Table 3. The CAT-A is more diesel selective while catalysts B&C are more selective to kerosene. There is a substantial increase in kerosene fraction from 45 % on CAT-A to 75 % on CAT-C with 30 % silica-incorporated alumina support. This again proves that the increase in the acidity of the catalysts results in higher cracking activity leading to increased kerosene selectivity.
